summary.note: approve + defect + verify + wording exceeds 20 because risk-identification and scope-statement are approved AND carry the missing-first-half note; risk-criteria and availability carry it as well and availability is also a defect.

style_ruling.rule: The ratified template carries BOTH halves: what the thing IS, then the teaching move. Four proposals in this batch are teaching-move-only.
style_ruling.applies_to: ISO defined terms an exam item can test on the definition - availability, risk-criteria, threat, vulnerability, nonconformity, residual-risk, confidentiality, integrity.
style_ruling.exempt: Terms whose name reads in plain English - risk-identification, scope-statement, lessons-learned. Teaching-move-only is acceptable there.
style_ruling.leak_consequence: Coverage is matched run divided by description length, so stating the definitional content IN OUR OWN WORDS and adding a teaching move dilutes coverage mechanically. This is a more robust failure mode than avoiding the definition, which loses the content. IT IS NOT A LICENCE TO PAD AROUND REPRODUCED TEXT - the definitional half is still written from scratch.

rows.note: Teaching move is strong - the consequence of omission propagating through the whole process. Missing the first half: never says what identification IS. Acceptable because the name reads in plain English. No change required.

Best in batch alongside nonconformity. One change: 'no organization is ever audited against it' -> 'certified against it'. An auditor may consult 27005; nobody is certified to it. More precise and more examinable.

Both halves present. 'actor or event' is a real addition over the ISO definition - threats are agents or events, and candidates conflate threat with vulnerability. Pairs correctly with the vulnerability row.

The timing point is the right teaching move and it is the failure an auditor actually sees. But risk-criteria is an ISO defined term and this never says what criteria ARE. Add the definitional half in our own words, per the style ruling.

'The property that fails with no attacker involved' is followed by 'a ransomware lock'. Ransomware is an attacker. Availability also fails WITH an attacker routinely - a DDoS is the textbook case. The insight underneath is right and worth keeping: availability is the property most often lost without an adversary. State that, not the absolute. Also add the definitional half - availability is an examinable defined term.
Correct that avoidance is the only one of the four that removes rather than shrinks or shifts. The benefit-forgone trade is the examinable point and it is not in the ISO definition.

'Both halves matter' - which halves? They were named by the description this replaces. Same class as the taskBlock defect from PROMPT-1B section 5: a sentence pointing at content the payload does not carry. Name them: use and management.
Good contrast - where control passes from configuration to physical means. The floor-plan-versus-reality point is the examinable one.
Best in batch. The three-part test is examinable, teachable, and appears in no standard's definition. 'Observation' is consistent with the corpus's own audit-findings row.
Both halves. 'Removing the opportunity, which is why it applies to trusted people' is the point candidates miss - they read segregation as a statement about distrust.
'A decision, not an omission' is the whole concept in four words, and the contrast with an untreated risk is exactly what an item would test.

Missing the first half but the name reads in plain English, so acceptable. 'Resolved against the organization' is a claim about audit practice rather than about the standard - defensible and useful at Foundation tier. Interfaces and dependencies is the right failure mode to name.

Both halves, plus the contrast that carries the examinable distinction - what remains because controls worked versus what remains because they were never finished. The explicit-acceptance point is 6.1.3.

rows.claim: clause 10 reads the omission as a gap in improvement
rows.note: I read this as A.5.27, Learning from information security incidents. Clause 10 is nonconformity and corrective action. FLAGGED, NOT ASSERTED - I got ISO 19011 wrong on exactly this kind of claim. Run it through check-citation-correspondence.mjs and report what the corpus says before applying.
'A review obligation rather than a joining-day one' is the examinable reframe and it is not in the control text.
Naming the threat model it is NOT for is the teaching move, and it explains the scope extension to home and shared workspaces without asserting a clause.

rows.claim: Clause 5.2 asks three separate things: documented, communicated inside the organization, available to interested parties where appropriate
rows.note: I read this as correct - 5.2 d, e and f. But it is a citation claim and every citation claim in this corpus goes through the instrument. Verify, then apply. 'Publishing a file satisfies only the first' is the examinable point.
'Closing a finding the day the fix ships proves only that it was applied' is the sharpest sentence in the batch after nonconformity.
'Cuts both ways' and then one way is given. Under-treatment is never stated. Either state both or drop the opener. The credibility-not-cost point is correct and should survive the fix.
'The half of a risk you can actually change' is the treatment-selection insight and it pairs correctly with the threat row. Good that the pair was written together.

gate_finding_outside_the_batch.hypothesis_to_test_not_to_assume: The interpolated 'or disclosed' splits the match into runs of roughly 5 and 4, and coverage is computed PER RUN rather than summed across runs in one description. If so, the 0.60 floor is defeated by a single interpolated word and every near-verbatim-with-one-edit reproduction in the corpus is invisible.
gate_finding_outside_the_batch.required: Run confidentiality and integrity through the gate with per-run detail printed. Report whether summed coverage across runs would have fired them. If it would, the fire list changes before batch 2 and possibly the scope.

pace_ruling.from: every row read by the director
pace_ruling.unconditional_exception: EVERY row whose description makes a clause, Annex or control-ID citation is read in full, regardless of the spot-read count. Both verification flags in this batch are citation claims, and that is where a defect is invisible to every mechanical check available.
pace_ruling.basis: 14 of 20 clean on a deliberately adversarial selection.
